submitted.rationale: Of the 3 measured compositions, index 21 (Sb 0.89) had the highest EQE at 0.0073%. Index 16 (Sb 0.81) gave 0.0032% and index 6 (Sb 0.40) gave 0.0031%. XRD shows the same peak set (Q≈2.79, 4.55, 5.33 Å⁻¹) at every composition, and it matches no listed phase well. MEGNet band gaps did not clearly separate the regions, so the choice rests on the measured EQE.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.0032% EQE, below index 21, even though MEGNet predicts a near-zero gap for ZnSb4O9
Measured 0.0031% EQE; the Zn3Sb2O7 small-gap prediction did not lead to high activity
MEGNet HSE gap of 4.2 eV is too wide to absorb 2.7 eV photons

consultations.verdict: Weak support. MEGNet HSE gives ~2.0 eV for Sb6O13 (mp-684679), which is below the 2.7 eV photon energy. Sb-rich mixed-valence Sb oxides are the most plausible visible absorbers. ZnSb2O6 and Zn7Sb2O12 also predict ~1.95 eV, but these are probably underestimates. ZnSb2O4 predicts 4.2 eV, so it is inactive. The prediction can't separate the compositions much, so I'm sampling the Sb-rich end first.

Moderate support. MEGNet predicts a very small gap (~0 eV) for Zn3Sb2O7 (mp-1345267, Sb 0.4), which suggests defect or mixed-valence states that could absorb 2.7 eV light near this composition. The Sb-rich end (index 21) gave very low EQE (0.007%), so I'm moving toward the Zn-rich side and targeting Sb≈0.40 (index 6).

Support. MEGNet predicts a near-zero gap for ZnSb4O9 (mp-1041117, Sb 0.8). It is also the best (still weak) XRD match at index 21, which suggests absorbing states below 2.7 eV in the Sb≈0.8 region. The measurements so far favour the Sb-rich side, and GP-UCB ranks indices 15–17 highest. Index 16 (Sb 0.806) sits right at the ZnSb4O9 stoichiometry.
